findings.summary: The idle-peer sweep runs before the socket is drained, so a stall between Polls longer than peerIdleTimeoutMs drops every peer even though their datagrams sit in the receive buffer.
findings.scenario: A client (acceptUnknownPeers=false) hitches past 30 s, for example on a synchronous load or at a breakpoint. The next Poll removes its Connect peer first, then drops the server's queued datagrams as droppedUnknownSource, so the link is lost for good. A server in the same case re-creates every peer under a new PeerId.

findings.summary: DualStack() returns true for any IPv6 bind whose IPV6_V6ONLY=0 was accepted, including a specific address such as ::1 that can never reach IPv4. Connect to an IPv4 address then succeeds, but every Send fails silently.
findings.scenario: Open(bindAddress="::1") returns DualStack()==true. Connect("127.0.0.1", p) returns None and makes a peer. Every Send returns Sent but only bumps sendErrors. The Ipv6Loopback test (tests line 1117-1119) asserts this behaviour while its comment says IPv4 is unreachable.

findings.summary: The ITransport header was not updated: it still says the library has no sockets and native UDP is later work, and that Disconnect makes the other side see PeerDisconnected. UdpTransport now breaks that (an accepted deviation).
findings.scenario: A reader of Transport.hpp (lines 52 and 75) relies on the Disconnect contract and the 'no sockets' note. docs/netcode.html was updated to say the opposite, so the code comments and the docs disagree.
